name: What should I watch out for when building an ADU in hillside or view-sensitive areas like Rancho Palos Verdes?

mainEntity.name: What should I watch out for when building an ADU in hillside or view-sensitive areas like Rancho Palos Verdes?

acceptedAnswer.text:
In hillside or coastal‑influenced areas such as Rancho Palos Verdes, ADUs face stricter scrutiny around grading, drainage, stability, views, and sometimes height and appearance. Even with supportive state ADU laws, local review may look closely at how your unit affects slopes and neighbors. 

These sites often require more engineering and careful construction planning, which adds both time and cost compared with flat urban lots.

Key factors:
- Geotechnical conditions, retaining walls, and slope stability
- Height limits, story limits, and view protection rules
- Access for emergency vehicles and construction equipment
- Stormwater management and coastal or environmental overlays

If you’re on a slope, plan for more upfront due diligence: surveys, engineering, and conversations with the city. Choose a team that has documented experience building on hillsides so they can anticipate and solve access, drainage, and foundation challenges before they become emergencies.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hillside and view-sensitive areas like Rancho Palos Verdes often require more engineering and tighter rules on grading, height, access, and drainage for ADUs. Expect extra design and review steps, and hire a team experienced with hillside work so they can plan foundations, access, and stormwater correctly.
